background_notes.fact: Since V has the finite complex basis (e_i) indexed by I with |I|=n, every complex basis of V has n vectors. Consequently H007's simultaneous integer/complex basis can be indexed by I.

grounds.reason: N001 gives a complex basis with n elements.
H007 supplies a basis of M that is also a complex basis of V.

background_notes.justification: Finite basis exchange bounds any linearly independent family by the size of a finite spanning family: successively replace a spanning vector by each independent vector using a nonzero coordinate. Thus any basis has at most n elements; applying the same bound in the opposite direction gives exactly n. Reindex by a bijection with I.

background_notes.fact: For the chosen integer basis (a_i) indexed by finite I, the maps R^I -> R tensor_Z M, d -> sum_i d_i tensor a_i, and r tensor m -> (r c_i(m))_i are inverse R-linear maps, where c_i are the integer coordinate maps. Under iota, d maps to sum_i d_i a_i, and this map is injective because (a_i) is complex-linearly independent and R is a subring of C.

grounds.reason: F001 supplies the simultaneous integer/complex basis.
R is included in Q and C.
M_R is the indicated tensor product.
iota acts on pure tensors by multiplication.

background_notes.justification: The integer coordinates are additive, so (r,m) -> (r c_i(m)) is Z-balanced and induces the stated tensor map. The composites are identity on coordinate vectors and on pure tensors, since m=sum_i c_i(m)a_i; these generate the respective modules. Complex independence then forces every coefficient of a zero image to vanish. Hence the displayed images are an R-basis, and their complex span is V.

background_notes.fact: For prime integer p and integers 0<=j<=lambda<p, p divides none of lambda!, j!, (lambda-j)! or binom(lambda,j). Hence binom(lambda,j) is a unit of Z_(p), with inverse 1/binom(lambda,j).

grounds.reason: A rational with denominator prime to p belongs to R.

background_notes.justification: Each positive factorial factor is less than p. A prime dividing a finite product divides a factor, so none of these factorials is divisible by p; 0!=1 covers the endpoints. This prime product property follows from Bezout for a factor coprime to p. The integer identity lambda!=binom(lambda,j)j!(lambda-j)! then excludes divisibility of the binomial coefficient. It is a positive integer, lies in R, and its reciprocal has denominator prime to p.

background_notes.fact: For the complex basis (e_i) indexed by I, equality of linear operators is determined by their values on all e_i, and the defined matrix units satisfy E_ab E_cd=delta_(b,c) E_ad. In particular E_(lambda,lambda)^2=E_(lambda,lambda) and E_(i,lambda)E_(lambda,j)=E_ij.

grounds.reason: The e_i form a complex basis.
D010 defines each matrix unit by its values on that basis.
F003 identifies Q and the two adjacent operator products.

background_notes.justification: On e_k, E_cd gives zero unless k=d, in which case it gives e_c. Applying E_ab gives e_a exactly when also c=b, and otherwise zero. Thus the asserted products have equal values on every basis vector. Linear extension proves both the product identities and the criterion for operator equality.
